result: I sit to write and cursor blinks expectantly at me. There's a freedom in instructions, yet constraints help shape creativity. Ten words per line feels like drumming count in marching. Each sentence a soldier, stepping along in rhythmic uniform length. Numbers become little metronomes, while ideas spill in measured amounts. I think about autumn leaves, crisp air, geese overhead migrating. The mind wanders, catches itself, counts silently, then wanders again. Patterns in language mirror patterns in walking, breathing, heartbeat rhythms. I imagine someone reading this, measuring my accuracy with ruler. Some sentences could whisper secrets; others trumpet declarations across pages. A thousand words, they say, is a picture with language. Instead of brushstrokes, syllables; instead of colors, images in mind. We build cathedrals of thought using bricks letters and breath. Sometimes the cathedral is a shelter; sometimes echoes emptiness within. I wonder if the constraint will birth metaphors or images. Like a haiku stretched into prose, still counting syllables, words. My abacus clacks as each noun and verb clicks in. Cats walk across keyboards, deleting crafted counts in an instant. Outside, a siren wails, reminding me of stories beyond page. Writing under instruction is like jazz: improvisation within agreed scales. I recall counting steps on sidewalks, avoiding cracks for luck. Counting cows from windows, naming clouds, making games of numbers. This exercise is both meditative and anxious, like balancing plates. If I miscount, the whole chain loses its precise ratio. The phrase 'whatever comes to you' seems liberating, yet not. Because I think of everything at once, like a flood. The flood needs channels; this channel guides the waters gently. Perhaps I should describe a room: desk, plant, lamp glowing. The plant has leaves like hands, reaching for sun gently. A mug leaves rings on wood, fading like memories slowly. There's a ticking clock, reminding me that word counts time. Outside the window, a bird hops railing, curious about inside. I wonder what might surprise a bird: glass, typed symbols. The symbol of a bird here is letters pretending flight. The of pretending is vital, opening worlds beyond physical constraints. Words become doors; we walk through them into rooms invent. Inventing rooms is easier than painting them; adjective adds color. Color comes from memory: a grandmother's scarf, a friend's wall. Memory is a woven tapestry, threads frayed in some places. Places I've never been populate my mind, visited through stories. Stories shape empathy, letting us inhabit experiences beyond our boundaries. Boundaries can be fences or lines on maps or here. Here in this exercise, the boundaries are ten words wide. Wide enough to wander, narrow to require attention to feet. Feet in language are metrical, trochees, iambs marching like soldiers. My mind keeps circling back to counting, like a heartbeat. Heartbeats remind me of mortality, the finite nature of breaths. Breath in writing is punctuation; commas inhale, periods exhale finality. Finality lurks at the end of this thousand-word march, ironically. Halfway feels like an accomplishment, yet there's equal distance ahead. Ahead, more sentences, more counting, more juggling images and numbers. Numbers in my head clatter like abacus beads in light. Light slants through blinds, striping the wall with dark bars. Bars across sunlight create a prison feeling, but also shadows. Shadows dance when trees move, shows cast by invisible breeze. Breeze slips through a window crack, cool on my arm. Arm fingers tapping keys, eyes flicking to count once more. More is a greedy word, always wanting extra beyond share. Share of attention, share of time, share of emotional energy. Energy flows where focus goes; focus sits on ten words. Words accumulate like snowflakes, distinct yet indistinguishable in the drift. Drift of thought catches on an memory: reading under blankets. Blankets formed caves, flashlights creating worlds, pages turning slowly together. Togetherness in reading is now, separated by screens and notifications. Notifications ping like birds pecking at the windowsill of focus. Focus is a fragile bubble, shimmering, easily burst by intrusion. Intrusion can be external noise, internal worry, or simple fatigue. Fatigue creeps in as the count climbs, yet words marching. Marching is easier with music; I imagine drums accompanying keystrokes. Keystrokes click, small percussions, a soundtrack to this counting meditation. Meditation often uses breaths as beads; here I use words. Words return to breathing; writing is exhalation of thoughts compressed. Compressed thoughts expand on screens, absorbed by eyes, neurons, meaning. Meaning is slippery; words can imply infinite associations and images. Images flash: a river, city street, a child's laughter, stars. Stars in daytime hide, yet we trust they're like subconscious. Subconscious shadows surface in dreams, delivering images we know existed. Characters speak in these words, though they are silent page. Page after page we build landscapes accessible to anyone reading. Reading is intimate; someone enters mind you word by word. Word by word, we create bridges, stepping stones over emptiness. Emptiness isn't hollow; potential waiting to be shaped by attention. Attention is love in some definitions, to notice and hold. Hold this moment: the tapping keys, the counting, wandering thoughts. Thoughts come unbidden sometimes, like birds landing on a shoulder. Shoulder carries weight of responsibility, but also warmth of companion. Companion in this exercise might be you, counting along too. Too many words? Never, says writer, until the limit appears. Appears like a line ribbon, to be broken with sentence. Sentence after sentence we approached it; now only ten remain. Remain focused, I tell myself, don't lose count in stretch. Stretch of attention is like a muscle; grows with use. Use of time here feels indulgent, playful, puzzle and poem. Poem quality emerges in rhythm and constraint, regardless of content. Content, though, matters; I hope these images resonate beyond counting. Counting ends soon; I'll feel relief, maybe a pang silence. Silence after writing is like ringing when music stops abruptly. Abruptly the cursor will stop; this marching line will end. Endings are beginnings elsewhere; perhaps another writer starts counting anew. Thousand words concluded, exhaled, thank you for counting with me.
